safety_intent.description: one-sentence natural-language statement of the safety property in plain terms, independent of variable names. Injected as a header comment into runner/ld_to_st.py's ST rendering of an XML-bodied variant, since a hand-authored .st file's own comment does not exist for those; see ml/README.md's XML-only benchmark idiom-drift discussion for why this field exists.

syntax_pair_of.description: id of the twin benchmark in the other syntax, if this is a syntax-coverage pair

semantics.description: The execution-model assumptions under which the expected verdicts hold. A disagreement between two tools can be a semantic difference, so the assumptions are part of the benchmark definition.

scan_order.description: Order in which rungs or statements are evaluated within one scan.

retained_state.description: State that carries over between scans.

timer_counter_model.description: How timers and counters are modeled; present when the program uses them.

arithmetic.description: Arithmetic assumption such as H1 (no integer overflow); present when a SAFE verdict is conditional on it.

enum: holds under the stated scan order

validation_status.description: validated = every variant agreed with the expected verdict on two ESBMC routes that share no front end (the ladder front end and the Beremiz/MATIEC route); candidate = not promoted under that rule, with a verdict that rests on construction or fault injection (many depend on timer or counter semantics)

expected_verdict.description: true = SAFE (all properties hold); false = VIOLATION
